title: How to Create a Retirement Income Ladder Using CDs and Treasuries
description: Building a guaranteed paycheck for the first 5-10 years of retirement.
content:
A 'Bond Ladder' is the ultimate sleep-aid for retirees. Instead of relying on bond funds (which fluctuate in price), you buy individual bonds or CDs that mature exactly when you need the money. By stacking these maturities—one expiring in 2026, one in 2027, one in 2028—you create a guaranteed income stream that bridges the gap to Social Security or allows your stock portfolio to recover from a crash. This guide explains how to construct a 5-10 year ladder.

Key Takeaways

  • Principal Certainty: If you hold a Treasury Bond to maturity, you get 100% of your principal back + interest. Market price fluctuations along the way do not matter. This eliminates 'Interest Rate Risk'.
  • Expense Matching: If you need $40,000/year from your portfolio, you buy a $40,000 bond maturing each year. You have mathematically funded your life for the duration of the ladder.
  • Treasuries vs CDs: Treasuries are state-tax free. CDs are not. For high earners or those in high-tax states, Treasury ladders usually offer a higher effective yield.
  • The 'Rolling' Strategy: As Year 1 matures and is spent, you can sell stocks (if up) to buy a new Year 6 rung, perpetuating the ladder.

Why It Matters (US Context)

You can build ladders easily at Fidelity or Schwab using their 'Fixed Income' tools. You do not need to use TreasuryDirect.gov. Brokered CDs also allow you to hold FDIC-insured CDs from multiple banks in one account.

The Ladder Blueprint

Goal: $50,000 income for 5 years ($250k total).

The Purchase (Day 1)

  • Rung 1: $50k in Money Market (Liquid for Year 1).
  • Rung 2: $50k in 2-Year Treasury Note (Matures Year 2).
  • Rung 3: $50k in 3-Year Treasury Note.
  • Rung 4: $50k in 4-Year Treasury Note.
  • Rung 5: $50k in 5-Year Treasury Note.

Result: You have successfully immunized your income against stock market crashes for 5 years. Even if the S&P 500 drops 50%, your paycheck arrives on schedule.

The Yield

You also earn interest. If rates are 4%, you generate ~$10,000/year in interest on top of the principal return. This fights inflation.

Execution Tips

  1. Use 'Defined Maturity' ETFs: If buying individual bonds is scary, use iShares iBonds or Invesco BulletShares ETFs. These are funds that hold bonds maturing in a specific year (e.g., '2028 Corporate Bond ETF'). They liquidate and return cash in Dec 2028.
  2. Call Protection: When buying CDs, ensure they are 'Non-Callable'. Callable CDs can be cancelled by the bank if rates drop, destroying your ladder. Treasuries are always non-callable.
  3. Auto-Roll vs. Spend: If you are building the ladder before retirement, set it to 'Auto-Roll' (reinvest). If you are in retirement, set it to pay out to cash for spending.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why not just buy a Total Bond Fund?

Funds (BND) have no maturity date. If rates rise, the fund value drops. If you need to sell BND to pay bills during a rate spike, you lose money. A ladder guarantees par value.

How long should the ladder be?

5 years is standard. It covers the average length of a bear market (2-3 years) with a safety margin. Extending to 10 years reduces inflation protection.

Can I sell early?

Yes, Treasuries and Brokered CDs are liquid. But you will sell at market price, potentially taking a loss. Only sell if it's an emergency.
